title: Israel's Histadrut union calls a general strike after six hostages are found dead
body:
On Monday 2 September 2024, Israel's largest trade union, Histadrut, called a nationwide general strike to pressure Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu to reach a ceasefire and hostage deal. The strike followed the recovery by the Israeli military of the bodies of six hostages from a tunnel in the Rafah area of Gaza. It was the first such strike since the Hamas-led attack of 7 October 2023.

The strike closed many schools and government buildings, paused flights at Ben Gurion airport for several hours, and led many private businesses to shut in solidarity, although not all regions or businesses took part. Israel's Labor Court ordered the strike to end by 2:30 p.m. local time, and Histadrut complied and called it off. On Sunday 1 September, crowds had packed central Tel Aviv, blocking several major intersections.

Israel's Health Ministry said Hamas killed the six hostages with short-range gunshots in the days before they were found. Netanyahu said that whoever murders hostages does not want a deal and that Hamas had refused all proposals. Protesters and families of hostages said chances to bring the hostages home had been missed. Negotiations had stalled for months, with Netanyahu refusing to give up Israeli control of the Philadelphi corridor. Gaza's Health Ministry reported at least 40,786 deaths in the war at that point.
